To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a new conditional analysis method for multiple quantitative traits based only on marginal summary statistics of genome-wide association studies, which is useful for fine mapping and for distinguishing direct and indirect effects.
we have developed a method for conditional analysis of multiple traits based on marginal genome wide summary statistics, and demonstrated the effectiveness of our method by numerical examples.

we propose a novel conditional analysis of multiple quantitative trait GWAS summary statistics based on a joint linear model and provide necessary calculations to fit such a model, and we show by numerical examples that our proposed approach offers a more powerful and informative analysis than standard marginal analyses.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a conditional analysis of multiple quantitative trait GWAS summary statistics, and the method we propose is expected to be a valuable tool to help better understand complex genetic architecture of multiple quantitative traits.
a conditional analysis of quantitative traits based on only GWAS summary statistics, which is a new problem and has important applications in genetic epidemiological studies.
the conditional analysis of multiple traits based on marginal association test statistics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our method is the first to offer a conditional analysis on multiple quantitative traits based only on GWAS summary statistics.
our proposed method is a useful tool for joint analysis of multiple quantitative trait GWAS summary statistics.
our proposed conditional analysis can provide useful information for understanding genetic architecture of multiple quantitative traits.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our proposed method is able to identify a SNP that has a significant direct effect on a trait, but not on other traits, or a significant indirect effect of a SNP on a trait via another trait.

we have provided a novel method for conditional analysis of multiple quantitative phenotypes using GWAS summary statistics, and our approach can be useful for fine-mapping and understanding of the biological mechanism of genetic associations with multiple traits.
we provide a new tool for a conditional analysis of quantitative traits, which can be useful to identify direct and indirect effects, or to further refine a region of interest for a fine mapping.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the presence of a pleiotropic genetic variant, conditional analysis of multiple quantitative trait can be useful in identifying the direct effects of the genetic variant on the traits, while marginal analysis may only reveal the indirect effects of the variant.

, with only GWAS summary statistics, we are able to conduct conditional analysis of multiple quantitative or qualitative traits, which is useful for understanding the causal relationship among traits and for fine mapping.
conditional analysis of multiple quantitative phenotypes is feasible with GWAS summary statistics and may offer additional insights to better understand the genetic basis of multiple phenotypes.
